title: RedWork: follow-up on declined repair work for independent garages
summary: Garages find urgent ("red") and advisory ("amber") faults during inspections, but most drivers leave without approving all of it. RedWork sends timed, personal follow-ups with the photos and video from the inspection, offers a booking slot and tracks how much declined work comes back.
hook: "We told him the brake pads were down to 2 mm. He said next month. We never heard from him again."
story:
**Mehmet runs an independent garage with 4 bays and 6 technicians.** Every day his team does health checks and finds red and amber items: worn tyres, brake pads, leaking shock absorbers. Most customers say "not today". The work is written in the job card and then forgotten. His garage software can send a yearly MOT reminder, but nothing for **declined work**.

He tried calling customers back, but nobody has time on a busy day. A simple system that sends the right message at the right time (pay-day, two weeks later, before winter) with the **photo of the worn part** and a link to book could bring back a few jobs a week. At an average of **£250 per job**, that pays for the tool many times over.
whyNow: Drivers are under cost pressure: a 2026 analysis found that in 70% of health checks with red items, drivers did not approve all urgent work, mostly because of cost. Garages already take photos and videos in digital health checks, and WhatsApp/SMS messaging plus AI-written messages make personal follow-up cheap.
evidence: In 70% of vehicle health checks with red items, drivers did not approve all urgent work; 46% said they could not afford it (vendor data) [Bumper / AutoBI]
47% of affected drivers did not approve advisory (amber) items (vendor data) [Bumper / AutoBI]
UK franchised dealers left an estimated £480 million of red work unsold in 2016, about £99,200 per dealer [AM Online]
A dealer case study reported an 86% rise in amber work approved after automated follow-up (vendor case study) [CitNOW]
UK garage management tools with digital inspections cost about £25–149 a month, e.g. £149/month flat for EZ Garage and Garage Desk [GetApp / GarageWire]

sources.title: Bumper: drivers leave workshops with urgent repairs incomplete
AM Online: dealers missing out on £99,200 in lost sales
AM Online: dealers lose revenue with poor VHC management
GarageWire: new garage management system at £25 a month

whyReal.title: Money already found, then lost
whyReal.text: The garage has done the inspection and found the fault. The only missing step is asking again at a better time.

whyReal.title: Most declined work is about cash flow
whyReal.text: Drivers say "not today" because of money, not because they disagree. A reminder after pay-day or with a split-payment option often works.

whyReal.title: Garage tools focus on the job, not the follow-up
whyReal.text: Garage software handles bookings, invoices and MOT reminders. Declined-work follow-up is usually a report nobody reads.

whyReal.title: Easy to prove ROI
whyReal.text: Every recovered job is visible in pounds or euros, which makes the sale simple for Jonatan.

whoPays.label: Customer
whoPays.text: independent garages and small chains (2–15 technicians), tyre and service centres.

whoPays.label: Start market
whoPays.text: UK (red/amber health-check culture), then Ireland, Nordics, Australia and the rest of the EU.

solution.title: Capture declined items
solution.text: import declined lines from the garage software (CSV, email report or API) or let the technician tap them in the app with a photo.

solution.title: Plan the follow-up
solution.text: rules choose the timing: red items after 3–7 days, amber items before the season or the next service.

solution.title: Personal messages
solution.text: AI writes a short, friendly SMS/WhatsApp message in the garage's voice, with the photo or video and a booking link.

solution.title: Easy booking
solution.text: the driver picks a slot; the garage gets the job with the original inspection notes.

solution.title: Recovery dashboard
solution.text: shows declined value, recovered jobs and money earned each month.

later: API integrations with popular garage software
Google review requests after the job

timeline.what: **Validate, no code.** Jonatan visits 15 garages and asks for last month's declined-work list; we send follow-ups by hand for 2 garages.
Import, rules, message drafting and sending.
Show recovered revenue to the pilots; convert to paid.

costs.note: Messages billed per use, passed on

pricing.name: Busy: €99/mo
pricing.description: Up to 500 follow-ups, booking link, dashboard

risks.risk: Garage software adds the same feature
risks.answer: Be the specialist that works with any system; partner with GMS vendors as an add-on.
Limit to 2–3 messages per item, use the garage's name and real photos, easy opt-out (GDPR/PECR).

risks.risk: Getting data out of old systems
risks.answer: Start with CSV/email reports; mobile entry as fallback.

risks.risk: Most evidence is from dealers and vendors
risks.answer: Measure recovery in the 2 hand-run pilots before building.
